result.title: Spend the Bits Where the Tiny Objects Are: Rate-Utility Region Coding for Aerial Detection
result.summary: Bandwidth-limited aerial cameras must compress their images before a remote detector can find the many tiny objects in them. Threshold-based region-of-interest (ROI) coding sends only confidently detected regions, and because tiny objects provide limited visual evidence and often score low, it can discard the regions that contain them. We propose rate-utility region coding (RUO), which sends a region when its expected detection utility justifies its measured byte cost, choosing to drop it or to send it at low or high quality with one multiplier shared across images. RUO trains no model, uses a standard image codec and decodes in a few milliseconds. On all 1,610 VisDrone-DET test-dev images, RUO uses 42.4% fewer bits than a tuned threshold-based ROI coder, averaged over their shared tiny-object average precision (AP) range. RUO also needs fewer bits for tiny objects than the AV1 Image File Format (AVIF), High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) and three published learned codecs, and its advantage over threshold-based ROI coding persists when the sender and receiver use different detectors. For AP over all object sizes RUO needs 25.4% more bits than the tuned ROI coder, because its allocation drops large regions first at low rates, so it suits tasks that target tiny objects. We plan to release the code.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 rate-utility region coding（RUO），按「期望检测效用是否抵得上实测字节成本」逐区域决定丢弃或低/高质量发送，用于带宽受限的航拍小目标检测，在 VisDrone 上以更少比特取得同等小目标 AP。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「效用—成本」区域取舍规则与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、LOOK/STOP 的计算预算决策有概念类比，可供核查；但该工作处理的是图像压缩传输而非内部 latent 状态，联系较远。
